interest: This file offers a fascinating glimpse into how the U.S. State Department monitored Japanese cultural heritage, historical manuscripts, and political memoirs during the 1930s. Of particular diplomatic significance is the 1935 report documenting Adolf Hitler's gift of a fourteenth-century Japanese painting—originally from Kyoto and held in a Prussian museum—to Emperor Hirohito (the Mikado) via Ambassador Mushakoji, highlighting how cultural diplomacy and art repatriation were deployed to foster German-Japanese rapprochement prior to the Anti-Comintern Pact. The file also demonstrates the U.S. government's close interest in Japanese diplomatic historiography through its tracking of the English translation of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's memoirs, alongside religious and cultural preservation efforts concerning sacred Buddhist relics like the Daihannyakyo.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.412) from the U.S. State Department's Records Relating to Internal Affairs of Japan spans June 1931 to July 1936 and concerns Japanese history, historical relics, and manuscripts. It consists of four pages comprising diplomatic despatches and cross-reference sheets from the American Embassy in Tokyo and the American Embassy in Berlin. Key subjects include the progress of translating Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs' (Gaiko Yoroku) into English, Chancellor Adolf Hitler's diplomatic gift of a fourteenth-century Kyoto painting from a Prussian museum to Emperor Hirohito via Ambassador Kintomo Mushakoji, and the transmission of photographs of the 'Daihannyakyo' (Great Prajnaparamita Sutra), an important Buddhist historical relic.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning the translation and publication status of Viscount Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs'.
subfiles.summary: This document file note references despatch No. 245 from Japan (Edwin L. Neville), indexed under 894.44 Ishii, Viscount/4. It records that an English translation of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's book 'Diplomatic Memoirs' is currently underway. However, it notes that no arrangements have yet been made for its publication.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding Viscount Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs'

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch reporting on the English translation status of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs'.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: In response to Department instruction No. 95 of April 9, 1931, Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville reports on information obtained from Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's secretary. The secretary stated that Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs' (Gaiko Yoroku) were being translated into English. Neville adds that no completion date could yet be established and no publication arrangements had been made.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 245 from Tokyo on translation of Viscount Ishii's 'Diplomatic Memoirs'

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning Adolf Hitler's gift of a fourteenth-century Japanese painting to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.summary: This document file note references despatch No. 2124 from Ambassador William E. Dodd in Germany, indexed under 762.94/63. It reports that Adolf Hitler presented a fourteenth-century Japanese painting to Japanese Ambassador Kintomo Mushakoji as a gift for the Mikado (Emperor Hirohito). The artwork had originally come from Kyoto and ended up in a Prussian museum, and its return was made in connection with fostering German-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding Hitler's gift of a 14th-century Japanese painting to the Mikado

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning photographs of the 'Daihannyakyo' Buddhist relic.
subfiles.summary: This document file note references despatch No. 1303 from Tokyo, indexed under decimal file 012.1/1516. It documents the receipt or transmission of photographs depicting the 'Daihannyakyo' (Great Prajnaparamita Sutra). The item is specifically identified as an important historical relic of the Buddhist religion.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding photographs of the 'Daihannyakyo' Buddhist relic
